title: Power Pages: MCP server exposes site data to AI clients
summary: The briefing's roadmap dates, licensing qualifications and documented configuration controls are supported. The site-visibility policy is correctly distinguished from the separate delegation setting, and the searches found no documented tenant-wide MCP switch.

claims.claim: MCP setup supports Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft Entra External ID.
claims.quote: This article shows you how to set up Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft Entra External ID as an identity provider for your Power Pages site and configure it to expose the MCP scope.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The MCP/Enabled site setting with value true enables the site's MCP server.
claims.quote: | Enable MCP server | `MCP/Enabled` | `true` | This site setting enables or disables MCP server for the site. |

claims.claim: A Copilot Studio agent can connect to the MCP endpoint and be published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This will create a new agent that we will publish later to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Web API access is limited to the tables exposed through its site settings.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose.

claims.claim: Web API access is limited to the columns exposed through the Web API.
claims.quote: You can define the columns available to the Web API by listing them in a site setting, by using a Dataverse system view, or by combining both methods.

claims.claim: Column permissions can further restrict Web API access.
claims.quote: You can configure column permissions to further define privileges to individual columns within a table while using the portal Web API.

claims.claim: The endpoint uses OAuth scopes and bearer-authentication settings.
claims.quote: This site setting defines the OAuth 2.0 scopes that the Power Pages runtime requests when authenticating an MCP client.

claims.claim: Incorrect site-setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly.
claims.quote: Incorrect site setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly. Double-check all entries before proceeding.

claims.claim: In Power Pages Management, Site Settings > New creates a site-setting record.
claims.quote:
Select Site Settings from the Portal Management menu.
Create the required site settings to enable and configure MCP server functionality. For each setting, select New to create a new site setting record.

claims.claim: pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <1-or-2> deploys changed site configuration rather than acting as a dedicated MCP toggle.
claims.quote:
After making the required changes, upload them using the pac pages upload command:
`pac pages upload --path [Folder-location] --modelVersion [ModelVersion]`

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The non-production public-access policy is at Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Manage.
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Select Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No API is documented for the non-production public-access policy as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin non-production visibility; Power Pages site visibility non-production API Set-TenantSettings. Opened site-visibility-governance and site-visibility: UI policy documented; PowerShell controls the separate system-administrator delegation setting.

claims.where: controls[3]; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Neither an admin UI nor an API tenant-wide switch for Power Pages MCP is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP tenant enabled inventory admin center; Power Pages MCP tenant settings PowerShell API. Opened MCP overview and site-settings setup; read Get-TenantSettings and Set-TenantSettings search excerpts. No tenant-wide MCP switch found.

claims.claim: MCP enablement is configured separately for each site.
claims.quote: This site setting enables or disables MCP server for the site.

claims.claim: No admin-center inventory field identifying MCP-enabled sites is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP inventory; Power Pages MCP tenant enabled inventory admin center. Opened power-pages-inventory and read its site-field list; read coe-portals inventory fields in search results. Neither lists an MCP-enabled field.

claims.claim: Site settings can also be edited through the Portal Management app.
claims.quote:
Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.
To edit an existing setting, select the Site Setting listed in the grid.

claims.claim: The separate tenant setting enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility controls System administrator permission to change site visibility.
claims.quote: When the tenant-level setting `enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility` is set to `true`, members of the System administrator security role can change the site visibility.

claims.claim: When that setting is false, System administrators must belong to an exclusive Microsoft Entra security group with site-visibility permissions.
claims.quote: If the tenant-level setting `enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility` is set to `false`, members of the System administrator security role must be a member of an exclusive security group in Microsoft Entra that has the permissions to manage site visibility.

claims.claim: The documented permissions setup adds MCP, openid and profile scopes and grants admin consent.
claims.quote:
Select the check box next to MCP and select Add permissions.
select the check boxes next to openid and profile, and then select Add permissions.
Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant], and then select Yes to finish the permissions setup.
